slides.headline: A second reader the agent cannot skip
slides.sub: On 9 October two emails drafted by an agent went out signed with the author's name. The fix was built that day.

slides.headline: Why a rule written four times failed
items: Only the agent's memory enforced it
The agent was the only reader of its draft
The rule was lost when the conversation was summarised

slides.headline: Every draft now passes through a guard
slides.sub: Anything else denies the draft. Every verdict is logged.

slides.headline: The checker gets less than the author, on purpose
items: A different model: Sonnet checks Opus
Only the rules, the sources and the draft

slides.quote: An email that is late is a small cost. An email that goes out wrong cannot be taken back.
slides.who: The inbox agent, on failing closed

slides.label: invented claims caught on the first run
slides.sub: Statements presented as the author's view or promise that were not in anything he had said.

slides.headline: Where the hook lives decides what it is
slides.sub: Same code, different owner. Only the last is a control.

slides.headline: Banks call it maker-checker
slides.sub: Segregation of duties, the two-person rule, the independent double check. The idea is old; the agent version now has a precise shape.

slides.headline: Put a gate on the call that matters
slides.sub: Code checks first, then a fresh checker. Deny on anything but an explicit PASS. Log every verdict.

Clean editorial infographic, cream background #faf9f5, rose accents, simple flat icons, no photographs. A portrait slide titled 'The checker gets less than the author, on purpose'. On the left, a small author figure surrounded by a long conversation scroll, a toolbox and a large pile of context. On the right, a checker figure with a tidy desk holding only three items: a short rules card, a sources folder and the draft. Four short cards run down the slide: a crossed out speech bubble, 'No conversation history'; a crossed out toolbox, 'No tools'; two different model icons side by side, 'A different model: Sonnet checks Opus'; and three neat documents, 'Only the rules, the sources and the draft'. Calm, minimal, legible, rose used sparingly, no other text or figures.

The quotation, in a large italic serif, reads: 'An email that is late is a small cost. An email that goes out wrong cannot be taken back.' Beneath it, two small flat icons side by side as a quiet gloss: an envelope with a small clock, labelled 'late', and an envelope flying away beyond a one way arrow, labelled 'wrong'. Clean editorial infographic, cream background #faf9f5, rose accents, simple flat icons, no photographs. A portrait statistics slide built around a single large rose serif numeral, '4', with the label 'invented claims caught on the first run' beneath it. Below the label, four small speech bubble icons, each with a rose flag attached, stand for the four claims, and a short line explains that these were statements presented as the author's view or promise that were not in anything he had said. To one side, a small checker figure holds a magnifying glass over a sources folder. Keep the numeral dominant and the rest quiet. No percentages, no other statistics, no names, no logos.

Clean editorial infographic, cream background #faf9f5, rose accents, simple flat icons, no photographs. A portrait diagram titled 'Where the hook lives decides what it is'. Four rounded white boxes with rose outlines, stacked top to bottom, joined by downward rose arrows with small italic labels. Top: a thought bubble, 'Expectation: agent's memory'. Arrow 'the hook'. Next: a folder inside a session window with a pencil the agent holds, 'Setting: session mod'. Arrow 'install it'. Next: a package from a repository with a small user badge, 'Setting: installed plugin'. Arrow 'manage it'. Bottom: a locked cabinet with an administrator key, drawn with a heavier rose outline, 'Boundary: managed settings'. A short line at the foot reads 'Same code, different owner', noting that only managed placement puts it out of the agent's reach. Clear hierarchy, legible labels.

Clean editorial infographic, cream background #faf9f5, rose accents, simple flat icons, no photographs. A portrait statement slide. The serif headline reads 'Banks call it maker-checker'. Beneath, a simple central motif of two figures, one preparing a document and a different one approving it, joined by a rose arrow. Around them, three small labelled icons in a loose arc show the same idea in other fields: a bank building with 'segregation of duties', two keys turned together with 'the two-person rule', and a medicine bottle with two tick marks for 'the independent double check'. A short line reads that the idea is old, and that the agent version now has a precise shape. Calm, balanced, no dates or numbers, no logos.
